title: Search queries are being rejected
briefing: A subset of catalog searches fails. Identify which check would best narrow the query failures.

actions.label: Compare index cutover cohorts
actions.criteria: Use when query errors appear close to an index switch and cohort isolation can test the relationship.
actions.instructions: Compare error rates for requests served by the old and new indexes.

actions.label: Inspect query and index field mappings
actions.criteria: Use when rejection evidence indicates a query field is incompatible with the active index schema.
actions.instructions: Compare the failing query fields with mappings in the old and new indexes.

actions.label: Inspect search shard capacity
actions.criteria: Use when queue depth, latency, or resource pressure suggests a capacity problem.
actions.instructions: Compare CPU, memory, and request queue depth across search shards.

fallback: Collect an affected search request and its serving index and response reason.

events.text: Search failure ratio doubled. The alert is grouped across query and index types.
At 06:31 UTC, 20% of the catalog search traffic began using catalog-v5. Other traffic still goes to catalog-v4.
The query gateway reports Q17 when a query sends a field incompatible with the index mapping. Q09 signals a shard request deadline.
Affected requests are grouped as reason=Q17, index=catalog-v5, field=variants.price. The baseline cohort is catalog-v4.

debrief.summary: The v5 mapping exposed variants.price as text while the numeric price filter still sent a range query. The new cohort made the error visible.
lessons: Cohort membership can reveal an incident caused by a genuine rollout regression.
Translate the gateway reason before choosing mapping inspection or capacity inspection.
